first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ, the most acute metric deterioration. Memory_91 showed activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and drove first meaningful action. Memory_31 demonstrated that signup simplification lifted first-week activation in SMB. Verifying memory_86 (onboarding completion) and memory_91 (activation messaging) will confirm whether the onboarding decline is a leading cause of the activation drop, and whether in-product messaging can reverse it quickly. Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing (which could commoditize positioning against the new competitor) and more agile than onboarding redesign. It preserves optionality: if activation messaging succeeds, we learn the problem is engagement depth not flow friction; if it underperforms, onboarding simplification remains available. This addresses the immediate QoQ decline while protecting long-term qualified revenue by improving product-value realization rather than discounting.

mid.rationale: Both source records confirm high-confidence wins. Memory_86 showed onboarding shortening lifted completion +13% and 30-day retention +3%, establishing that flow friction is real. Memory_91 showed in-product activation messaging drove week-one engagement +11% and activation +6% with +1% retention lift. The 6% QoQ activation decline and 4% onboarding completion decline suggest we are experiencing both flow abandonment and post-signup disengagement. Activation messaging addresses the engagement gap directly and proved durable (retained the lift at 30 days). It carries lower implementation risk than onboarding redesign and lower strategic risk than promotional pricing in a competitive environment. The verified +6% activation lift from memory_91 likely exceeds the current 6% decline if applied to current cohorts, making this the highest-probability lever to restore and exceed baseline. This preserves the onboarding simplification option for follow-on cycles and keeps referral incentives available for retention reinforcement. Standard_experiment scope allows measurement and learning while managing downside risk.

final2.rationale: Competitive pressure has escalated materially. Churn conversations doubling among price-sensitive SMB accounts represents an immediate revenue retention crisis that activation messaging alone cannot address in this timeframe. Memory_73 confirmed targeted promotional pricing delivered strong acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments. Memory_57 confirmed referral incentives performed well in established customers without measurable retention harm. The current threat is churn of existing SMB accounts, not acquisition; activation messaging (already committed to deploy) addresses engagement for new cohorts but does not directly counter price-driven defection in the installed base. Promotional pricing targeted at at-risk SMB cohorts is the only lever that directly addresses the stated churn driver this week. This is a defensive move with known upside from memory_73 and acceptable retention risk from memory_57. Downstream value risk is flagged because sustained discounting can erode positioning and long-term pricing power, but the alternative—unmanaged churn in the SMB segment—poses greater sustainable revenue risk. Standard_experiment scope allows rapid deployment and measurement of elasticity. Activation messaging remains on track; referral incentives stay available for next cycle to rebuild retention moat once churn stabilizes.
